newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks lifted, market seen mixed.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks lifted, market seen mixed.

text.p: Most Croatian stocks rose on Thursday in active trade dominated by Zagrebacka Banka but Friday was expected to be slower because of a brokers' meeting outside the capital.
Eleven of 16 issues rose, three fell and two were flat. Volume rose to 24,784 from 13,554 units, turnover jumped to 33.4 from 14.7 million kuna.
"Today's almost ten million German marks turnover is not an everyday occurrence," said one trader with a large market share, predicting mixed trends in the near future.
He pointed out Zagrebacka Banka and hotelier Laguna as likely to benefit from stronger investor interest.
Laguna shares rose 30 kuna to close at 1,480 on volume of 1,571.
"I'm not surprised that it's become more actively traded. Its is one of the best tourist firms on the Adriatic," the trader commented.
Zagrebacka's ordinaries fell 25 kuna to close at 2,035 although most of the 13,741 shares were sold at 2,050-2,070 kuna. They were the most active issue of the day.
"Zagrebacka Banka has dropped a lot and people expect it to rise again. I also believe it could firm slightly."
The other blue chip Pliva pharmaceuticals traded around 460 kuna with 1,724 shares sold and was seen as stagnating at that level.
"There is not much chance of Pliva's shares rising before we have some kind of news that will make this happen," the trader added.
Top gainer shipper Jadroplov added 55 kuna or almost 58 percent from late in May to 150 kuna, on volume of 322 shares, but this was seen as a freak increase.
Biggest decliner was hotelier Suncani Hvar, losing one kuna or 1.8 percent to 54 kuna with 332 shares sold.
Food stocks Kras and Podravka ended stable at 400 and 289 kuna on respectable volumes of 1,411 and 2,509, respectively.
But both were expected to hover around the current prices without prospects for a stronger growth for some time to come.
